recentItems.title: DZMM Radyo Patrol 630 new jingle [2025]
recentItems.description:
One of the most unexpected comebacks of 2025. ABS-CBN's once-successful radio station has come back on air. The audio was recorded from their online stream on their first night.

In this video is the new jingle from the new #DZMM Radyo Patrol 630 (formerly #DWPM Radyo 630), the sole AM station of Philippine Collective Media Corporation, a company owned by current Speaker of the House Martin Romualdez. Romualdez, a congressman from Tacloban City, is the cousin of current President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., whose late controversial father once had a bitter relationship with ABS-CBN.

0:00 - Instrumental
2:19 - Full jingle w/ vocals

Five years ago will forever be one of the darkest years for ABS-CBN. The company was hit with a cease-and-desist order on May 5th of that year when Republic Act 7966 expired. That is the congressionally-authorized law ("franchise" as it's referred to locally) granting them the ability to hold broadcast licenses across the country with a fixed 25-year expiration date. Unlike the United States for instance, the Philippines regulates broadcasters almost in the same way they would regulate local utilities—through a franchise granted by an act of Congress.

ABS-CBN applied for a renewal as early as during the administration of the late President Benigno Aquino III, and renewal bills were refiled during the administration of President Rodrigo Duterte. Congressional allies of both administrations largely ignored the network's application, with sources specifically citing their critical news coverage of the government in the country. With a government-allied supermajority in the lower House of Representatives, ABS-CBN was not only ignored until the last minute on their franchise application, but it eventually killed the network's franchise bids on July of 2020. Although the government used labor and tax issues as a key reason to reject the bid, critics and political commentators alike have attributed the network's shutdown to their coverage of Duterte's controversial drug war, with even Duterte allies calling the network "biased". This eventually led to the company laying off nearly 6,000 employees in late August.

Among the stations shut down was DZMM, the main backbone of the Radyo Patrol network of news/talk radio stations in the country, and Romualdez was among the 70 congressmen who voted to kill ABS-CBN's franchise bid. The Romualdez family itself is no stranger to the media business. Martin's father Kokoy founded People's Journal, one of the first newspapers to open during the martial law era. It was not necessarily a pro-Marcos publication, but it too faced heavy censorship. The Journal was initially sequestered by the new government of President Corazon Aquino (Noynoy's mother) after the People Power Revolution in 1986, in relation to their attempts at recovering the alleged stolen wealth of the Marcos family, but a court ruling forced the government to give back its shares of the paper to its original owners in 2004. The Romualdez family then acquired another paper, the Manila Standard, through a separate company in 2010. In addition, Martin's brother Philip is married to Sandy Prieto, proprietor of the Philippine Daily Inquirer, a traditionally independent newspaper often regarded as the record publication in the country.

As is the case when a new president is elected, the legislature's political allegiances change, and it resulted in a government that seemed to be slightly friendlier to ABS-CBN compared to previous administrations (and especially compared to the older Marcos Sr.), with Romualdez becoming the Speaker of the House. ABS-CBN's partnership with with Romualdez's PCMC started when PRTV, a local independent station in his district, started carrying programming from A2Z, one of many replacement channels for ABS-CBN programming.
